prompt: Design a developer tool dashboard — a home page showing project metrics, recent commits, active branches, and team activity, and an issue detail page with status, assignee, description, activity feed, and actions. Make it feel technical, clean, and modern.
title: Forgeboard

issues.description: The detail screen imports Input but does not render the required IssueCommentComposer component from the mount audit. The brief explicitly requires a labeled comment composer as the primary detail interaction, so the focused issue workflow is incomplete.

The detail Topbar receives an empty actions fragment and the screen does not render a working comment or issue-update CTA. The required primary action for adding a comment or updating the issue is therefore absent.

NAV contains only one item with id 'home', while detail.jsx sets activeId to 'detail'. The detail screen has no visible active navigation item or legal navigation path back to home, breaking the sidebar+topbar app navigation contract.

The measured layout reports four flush section transitions where adjacent sections are both 'border-b border-border bg-card'. This produces repeated flat panels separated only by hairlines, violating the deliberate-surface requirement and making the dashboard read as an assembled stack.

Card renders every panel as a flat card surface with only a bottom border: 'border-b bg-[var(--card)]'. When used across the home dashboard, adjacent sections become outline-only divisions rather than distinct bands, rows, or tonal surfaces.

The V17 density gate reports approximately 40% empty viewport on home, exceeding the 15% maximum for a feed context. The operations dashboard needs denser commit, branch, and team-activity rows without large unused vertical space.

The V17 deterministic gate reports a missing primary action on home. Although a 'New Issue' button is present in the Topbar, it is not wired to an action and the required ProjectOperationsToolbar create-issue affordance is not established as the screen's single working primary action.

The V17 density gate reports only two detail activity rows, below the required minimum of four. The issue timeline must show concrete comments, status changes, assignments, linked commits, or pull requests for this one issue.

The V17 density gate reports approximately 40% empty viewport on detail. The issue facts, activity timeline, and comment composer should occupy the available workspace with a focused, information-dense record view.

Geometry measurements report that the intended Sora font is not loaded. The resulting fallback changes the measured type scale and weakens the precise developer-tool hierarchy; load the configured font or correct the theme token.

Geometry measurements report that the intended Sora font is not loaded on detail as well. This should be corrected consistently across both verified screens rather than relying on an unplanned fallback.

The screenshot renders an API Service project detail page rather than the required focused issue detail. The dominant content is a project title and project-wide activity, while the screen intent requires one issue's identifier, title, status, description, facts, and issue activity only.

Required issue detail fields and controls are not visibly present: issue identifier, issue status control, priority, labels, repository, description, timestamps, edit/close actions, and assignment controls. The visible right-side project panel only shows generic project metadata.

The detail screen is scoped to the project 'API Service' and shows multiple project comments, not one selected issue record. This violates the one-item detail law and introduces unrelated project-wide data.

The detail view reads as a sparse generic white project page with a bordered metadata card rather than a dense developer-grade issue workspace. It lacks a clear issue title/status dominant moment and divided issue activity structure.

There is an approximately 900px empty vertical region between the sidebar/header area and the project content. This is an unsupported large blank gap and makes the screen appear broken rather than intentionally dense.
The rendered page is predominantly white with vivid default blue buttons and status accents, conflicting with the supplied dark Linear-inspired Forgeboard language and its restrained indigo accent.

The home dashboard has the same approximately 900px blank region above the operations header and health overview. The primary project operations content is pushed far below the viewport and does not read as an immediate dashboard.

TeamActivityFeed is visibly present only as six empty circular skeleton placeholders and blank rows. The required compact chronological team activity data is therefore missing, creating a sparse and unfinished section.

The project health overview does not visibly provide all required concrete health dimensions. Open issues, commit activity, and cycle time appear, but deployment status and a distinct pull request queue metric are absent; branch count is not a substitute for both.

The home screen uses bright default blue for the primary action, active navigation, chart, and PR pills, rather than the restrained indigo accent and monochrome-first palette specified for Forgeboard.

The dashboard is largely white and separated by repeated light-gray horizontal rules. It lacks the dark tonal bands and varied surface hierarchy expected by the supplied developer-grade design language, making the sections feel flat and assembled.

The toolbar and project content begin only after the oversized blank region, weakening the intended flow of compact project header, dominant health snapshot, trend, workstream rows, and team activity column.

reviewResult.summary: Forgeboard has the beginnings of the correct developer operations structure and uses relevant engineering vocabulary, but approval is blocked by the absent detail comment composer and primary action, broken detail navigation, repeated border-only home surfaces, and substantial density failures on both screens. The verified screens also use a missing theme font and do not yet satisfy the required focused issue workflow.
requiredFixes: Render IssueCommentComposer in src/screens/detail.jsx as the clearly labeled primary interaction, with a working submit handler.
Add legal navigation for both home and detail in src/lib/shell.jsx and ensure the sidebar exposes the current screen and a route back to the project dashboard.
Resolve the home density failure in src/screens/home.jsx by reducing unused viewport space and rendering the required workstreams and team activity at useful row density.
Replace adjacent border-only card sections in src/screens/home.jsx and src/components/Card.jsx with deliberate alternating surfaces and visible section spacing.
Increase detail activity content to at least four meaningful issue-specific timeline rows and use the available vertical space in src/screens/detail.jsx.
Load the intended theme font or update the theme token configuration so the Sora/font-not-loaded failure is removed and typography matches the design language.

Rebuild detail so it renders one issue record, including issue identifier, title, status, priority, assignee, labels, repository, description, timestamps, actions, activity timeline, and the comment composer.
Remove the approximately 900px blank region above the main content on both screens and place the application header and content within the intended desktop grid.
Replace the empty Team Activity Feed skeleton rows on home with real chronological issue, review, merge, deployment, and comment activity.
Apply the Forgeboard/Linear visual language consistently: dark developer workspace surfaces, monochrome styling, hairline divided rows, and restrained indigo rather than default bright blue controls.
